subject: Careers
title: Rights and responsibilities at work
calendar_note: Spring 2 runs 22 February to Thursday 25 March 2027. Friday P1 is taught 26 February, 5, 12 and 19 March. Week 5 has no Friday and no lesson. Week 4 is the taught closing review by owner brief.
timing: Agree a response mode and recall one useful idea.
Read the invented model; explain the key words; check understanding.
Work as reader and checker, swap roles, then answer the hinge privately.
Each learner gives their own response using a chosen route.
Review evidence, give one next step, keep the reply and save.
source_adaptation: Owner-supplied rows retained exactly. Rows 96–97 share Week 3; rows 98–99 share Week 4. Forty-minute phases, examples, activities and access are authored. No statutory rate, personal entitlement or future law claim.

sources.note: Exact scheme wording and Friday dates supplied in the owner brief. No underlying workbook bytes or fresh repository inspection claimed.

Edition and resource structure, generic invented paper-pack workplace and carried-forward workroom scene. Learner-facing route labels updated to Supported, Independent and Aspire; Standard and Stretch remain only in legacy filenames.

Supported: Work with cards A, B and C first. An adult can read one sentence at a time. Use the three headings and point to a choice.
Use these starts: 'The worker has a right to ...'; 'The worker should ...'; 'The employer should ...'. Match a right with the person who has to act.
For C, choose between guessing the method and pausing to ask for training. Explain by voice, pointing plus a short reason, usual aid or exact scribe. Then give your own help request.
Keep one sort choice and one safe request as evidence. Use the same success checks; fewer repeated cases and normal access help are valid.
Independent: Sort all six cards and explain two choices. Identify where more than one responsibility applies.
Give your own safe response to C or E. Name the person you would ask and a sensible next step if the concern continues.
Explain why a mistake or lateness does not remove a worker's rights. Use the information in D or F.
Aspire: Compare C and F. Explain why pressure to finish quickly or a concern about timekeeping cannot settle a safety or rights question.
Improve an unclear request: 'This is unfair.' Add the relevant facts, a safe request and the person who can help. Avoid claiming that every unfair feeling is unlawful discrimination.
Identify one limit of the information available. Explain why real advice needs the actual circumstances and employment status. More writing is optional.

business: An invented, unnamed small workplace prepares paper packs. A supervisor gives instructions; a preparer and checker share the task. Use ready-cut paper only. All workplace stories, contract terms and payslips are invented teaching examples. They are not records of a learner’s employment.
success_checks: Distinguish a workplace right from a responsibility using at least two examples.
Explain how an employer and a worker both help to protect safety.
Choose a safe, respectful way to raise a workplace concern and explain why.
teacher_grid_rule: Judgement cells initially blank. Review actual individual evidence. Keep learner self-review separate. A missing item or unticked outcome needs a recorded gap or follow-up, not an invented judgement.
private_help: Use voice, writing, pointing, a usual aid, typing or an exact scribe. Read back and correct. Plan in any language. Ask a trusted adult privately; pass, pause and return with support. No personal work or family story is needed.
feedback_rule: VF verbal feedback · WS worked with support · I independent · NS next step · // self-edit · ? read this back to me · E saved evidence · R responded. Keep the first try, one NS and the learner reply. Record R only after Voice and Audience are clear and the learner responds to NS in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to the Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any mapping to the unit award; no award completion is implied.
